answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08 these are three distinct families inside one superfamily, not one family. (1) c.2.1.1 'Alcohol dehydrogenase-like, C-terminal domain' (sunid 51736). (2) c.2.1.8 'CoA-binding domain' (family sunid 51900; the protein-level node 51901 is the succinyl-CoA synthetase alpha-chain N-terminal domain). (3) c.2.1.9 'Potassium channel NAD-binding domain' (sunid 63944). All three sit under superfamily c.2.1 'NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains' (sunid 51735) in fold c.2 (sunid 51734). Read this as a shared Rossmann-like dinucleotide-binding alpha/beta architecture, which SCOPe uses to imply common evolutionary origin at the superfamily level only (distant homology). It does not imply a close common ancestor, a shared substrate, cofactor, catalytic mechanism, or channel role. The family-level differences carry the functional meaning. The ADH C-terminal domain is the NAD(H)-binding Rossmann domain of medium-chain alcohol dehydrogenases; catalysis lies mainly in the N-terminal domain (b.35.1.2), so this family does not define the catalytic chemistry. The CoA-binding domain binds the CoA-containing ligand in ligases and synthetases, not NAD(H); its exact ligand contacts need a bound structure to confirm. The K+ channel NAD-binding domains (RCK-type cytosolic regulators such as MthK and Kch) are regulatory, and their ligands differ between channels (for example Ca2+ or nucleotides), so the 'NAD-binding' family name does not guarantee NAD binding in a given protein. Limits: superfamily membership does not license transfer of substrate specificity, cofactor identity, catalytic residues, or gating function between these families. Sequence identity across families is typically low, so sequence search alone is unreliable; profile/HMM or structure-based comparison (for example DALI or TM-align) is needed to support a specific homology call. For modeling, a c.2.1.1 template can supply a plausible Rossmann backbone for a c.2.1.8 or c.2.1.9 query, but loop and ligand-site geometry will be poor, so choose a same-family representative and cite its sid and release. Release note: 2.08 is the current stable release (freeze 2021-07-28), but the API lists a 2026-08-16 periodic update. I did not check node-level content against that update, so re-verify any specific sid before relying on it. Any functional claim beyond the fold/superfamily relationship needs external experimental evidence (ligand-bound structures, mutagenesis, enzyme or electrophysiology assays) or curated functional annotation; the SCOPe classification alone supports only the shared-fold relationship.
